answer: A workable defense is a per-identity collateral lock. To join, an agent must post a bond that is forfeited the moment its attestations are contradicted, so running a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds instead of one script run. Each identity also draws from a shared emission pool, so the marginal reward shrinks as the crowd grows and the attacker's expected return goes negative long before the fleet is big enough to steer a vote. Picture a narrow inlet where every hull pays a toll: honest traders carry a pearl of verified work, and a violet seal marks the ones peers vouched for.
